title: Impact of Close-Election Incumbency on Reelection Probability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Regression Discontinuity Design (sharp RDD)

• Method choice  
In very close elections the treatment (incumbent barely wins) is assigned by whether the vote-share margin crosses the deterministic cutoff of 0.  Observations infinitesimally to the left and right of the cutoff are plausibly identical except for the treatment, making RDD the natural causal design.

• Key identifying assumptions  
1. Continuity: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of future reelection probability is continuous in vote-share margin at the 0 cutoff.  
2. No precise manipulation: Candidates cannot sort themselves with perfect precision around the cutoff; hence the density of the running variable is continuous at 0.

If these assumptions hold, the jump in the outcome at 0 identifies the Local Average Treatment Effect of “barely winning” on the probability of winning the next election.

## 2. R Code
```r
# =====================================================
# Impact of Barely Winning on Subsequent Reelection
# =====================================================

# 0) Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)   # data wrangling / plotting
  library(rdrobust)    # state-of-the-art RDD estimation
})

# 1) Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s88_data.csv",
               col_types = cols())

# 2) Basic checks -----------------------------------------------------------
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(running = running_var,
         treat_calc = ifelse(running >= 0, 1, 0))

cat("Share where provided indicator equals calculated indicator: ",
    mean(df$treated == df$treat_calc), "\n")

# 3) SHARP RDD (local linear, MSE-optimal bandwidth) ------------------------
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running, c = 0)

cat("\n===== Main RDD result (local linear) =====\n")
print(rd_main)

# Extract and print the treatment effect at the cutoff
tau_hat  <- rd_main$coef[1]      # point estimate
se_tau   <- rd_main$se[1]        # robust std. error
p_value  <- rd_main$pv[1]

cat(sprintf("\nPoint estimate (τ̂) = %.4f\nStd. Error = %.4f\np-value = %.4f\n",
            tau_hat, se_tau, p_value))

# 4) Robustness: alternative bandwidths ------------------------------------
# half the optimal bandwidth
h_half <- rd_main$bws[1] / 2
rd_half <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running, c = 0, h = h_half)

# double the optimal bandwidth
h_double <- rd_main$bws[1] * 2
rd_double <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running, c = 0, h = h_double)

cat("\n--- Robustness: Half-bandwidth ---\n")
print(rd_half$coef[1:3])

cat("\n--- Robustness: Double-bandwidth ---\n")
print(rd_double$coef[1:3])

# 5) Robustness: higher-order polynomial (quadratic) -----------------------
rd_quad <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running, c = 0, p = 2)

cat("\n--- Robustness: Quadratic fit ---\n")
print(rd_quad$coef[1:3])

# 6) Placebo test: artificial cutoff at +0.05 ------------------------------
placebo_cut <- 0.05
rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running, c = placebo_cut)

cat("\n--- Placebo cutoff (+0.05) ---\n")
print(rd_placebo$coef[1:3])

# 7) McCrary density test for manipulation ---------------------------------
# (run only if rdrobust ≥ 1.0.7 which includes rddensity)
if(requireNamespace("rddensity", quietly = TRUE)){
  dens <- rddensity::rddensity(X = df$running, c = 0)
  cat("\n--- McCrary manipulation test ---\n")
  print(dens$test)
}

# End of script ------------------------------------------------------------
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive.  
Incumbents who barely win are expected to reap incumbency advantages (name recognition, fundraising, constituent services), making them more likely to win the following election.  

Magnitude: A local increase of roughly 10–20 percentage points in reelection probability (τ̂ ≈ 0.10–0.20). This range is consistent with the U.S. House close-election literature documenting effects from 5 pp to 25 pp depending on era and office.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We analyze the discontinuity at the vote-share cutoff to isolate the effect of incumbency.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Winning a close election reduces the probability of reelection.
